full_judgment:
2. These five criminal petitions for leave to appeal have been filed against the judgment and order dated 20-11-2016 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 2893 and 2895-2898 of 2016 disposing of all the Rules with some observations and directions. 

 3. Facts necessary to dispose these petitions are that the accused-petitioner obtained credit facility from the complainant bank. In order to discharge the loan liability, he gave separate cheques to the bank which, on presentation to the bank for encashment, were dishonoured on ground of insufficiency of funds. Following the procedures and in compliance of the statutory provisions laid down in section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (in short, the Act, 1881) the bank filed the respective CR Cases against the accused. The cases were ultimately transferred to the Court of Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Court No.3, Chittagong for disposal. 

 4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid proceedings of the sessions cases, the accused-petitioner filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos.2893 and 2895-2898 of 2016 before the High Court Division for quashing the proceedings not on the ground of any violation of the provisions of section 138 of the Act, 1881. Rather, the challenge was mainly on two separate grounds, firstly, the cheques are post-dated blank cheques which were given to the bank as security against the loan, and the bank subsequently filled in the cheques and used them at its own sweet will which, according to the petitioner, is illegal, and secondly, the bank has already filed Artha Rin Suit against the accused claiming the amount which also covers the value of the cheques in question. It has been argued that the bank is not allowed to pursue two separate proceedings for the same cause of action and for the same purpose, i.e. recovery of loan which amounts to double jeopardy and unjust enrichment. 

 "Hence, it is ordered that the proceedings of the respective CR Cases shall remain stayed till disposal of the Artha Rin Suit No.90 of 2012 now pending in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong. Adjournment sine die is not in accordance with law. Therefore, if the Artha Rin Suit is stayed or adjourned at the instance of the accused petitioner, the order of stay shall stand vacated and the proceedings of the respective CR Cases shall continue." 

 8. Upon consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the High Court Division observed, "We have already held that the criminal proceedings under the Act, 1881 cannot be throttled on the ground of pendency of the Artha Rin Suit." But nevertheless went on to dispose of the Rule in terms of the order quoted above. 

 9. The final conclusion of the High Court Division is contradictory to several decisions of this Division wherein it has been clearly held that the pendency of a civil suit will not hinder proceeding of a criminal case and vice versa. In this regard, reference may be made to the cases of Monzur Alam (Md) vs State, 55 DLR (AD) 62, SAB Solaiman Ali vs Rangs Industries Limited, 2004 1 Law Guardian (AD) 20. 

 In the light of the above decisions, we are constrained to hold that the impugned judgements and orders of the High Court Division are palpably erroneous and are hereby set aside. Accordingly, the criminal petitions for leave to appeal are disposed of with direction that both civil and criminal cases shall proceed in accordance with law.
